answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active association worker and 3 inactive workers. Draw 8 Zoo cards and keep 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards. Put Action cards side I up, with Animals in the leftmost slot (strength 1) and the other four randomly in the other slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, then 1, 2, and 3 in turn order.
answers.evidence: Personal setup: B places Animals under the leftmost slot, side I; C3 places 1 active worker and 3 lying down; D: Take 25 money; E: Draw 2 Final Scoring cards; F: Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4. Appeal track stagger: 0, 1, 2, 3 by turn order.

answers.answer: The setup has 3 face-up Base Conservation Projects except in a 4-player game, which has 4. In a 2-player game only, block the left level on the left project, middle level on the middle project, and right level on the right project, plus the donation area's three spaces in its left column. No such blocks are specified for 3 or 4 players. Deal the initial display face down and reveal its 6 cards after everyone chooses starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b: in a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up; otherwise the 3 topmost. Setup 5c: 2-player game only ... cover the left/middle/right levels ... and three spaces in the left column of the donation area. Personal setup G: after everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.

answers.answer: After using the slot-4 card, remove it, shift the cards that were left of that empty slot (slots 1–3) one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. Set strength before the action; each X-token spent adds 1 strength and returns to supply. You may spend any number, though strength above 5 may not improve some actions; you cannot hold more than 5 X-tokens, and tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. An after-finishing effect resolves after the action is complete, including moving its card.
answers.evidence: Taking a turn: remove the card from its slot, shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right, and place the used card in slot 1. X-tokens: each adds +1; you can never hold more than 5; set strength before performing the action. After finishing effects wait until the action, including moving Action cards, is complete.

answers.answer: You may not do nothing; if you cannot or do not want to perform a regular action, take exactly 1 X-token as the alternative action. Still select an Action card, move it to slot 1, and shift the intervening cards right; its strength and upgrade state do not matter. You cannot take this action while holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Taking a turn: You may not do nothing ... use the alternative X-token action. X-token action: take exactly 1 X-token; still select an Action card, move it to slot 1 and shift intervening cards; impossible if already holding 5.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional steps and the break occurs after the current turn ends. The player who reached it gets 1 X-token. They finish the rest of their turn before the break; after the break, play continues clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track: the break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get 1 X-token for reaching the last space. Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space. After the break ... play continues clockwise with the next player.

answers.answer: Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck per its strength table (up to 3, with a possible discard) or, at strength 5+, snaps exactly 1 display card of any reputation instead of drawing; replenish at turn end. Cards II also advances 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or display cards within reputation range, in any order, per its upgraded table. Its snap is available from strength 3 and takes exactly 1 display card regardless of reputation, with no deck draw. Reputation range restricts the side-II draw option, not snapping. Do not replenish the display until the turn is complete. There is no hand limit during a turn; discard to the limit only at breaks.
answers.evidence: CARDS action: Side I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then draw or snap at strength 5+; side II advances 2 and draws from deck and/or within reputation range; snapping works from strength 3. On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation. Display is not replenished until turn complete; hand limit is only checked during breaks.

answers.answer: Folders 1–6 cover reputation 1, 2–3, 4–6, 7–9, 10–12, and 13–15. Within reputation range means the folder matching your Reputation counter plus lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action. At 15, further reputation does not move the counter and instead gives 1 appeal per excess reputation step. You may not inspect the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation spaces and rewards: folders 1–6 correspond to reputation 1 / 2–3 / 4–6 / 7–9 / 10–12 / 13–15. ‘Within reputation range’ includes the matching folder and lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 further reputation gives 1 appeal per step. You may not look through the discard pile.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building, size no greater than strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in one action. Buildings cost 2 money per space. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by an edge. Build only on empty spaces, without extending off-map, overlapping, or covering water/rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Each kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately gives 1 appeal once.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: Side I exactly 1 building up to strength; Side II as many different buildings as desired, maximum total size strength and never 2 identical. Placement rules: first building on border; later adjacent; restricted-icon spaces require upgraded Build; kiosk at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion increases appeal by 1. Cost is 2 money per space.

answers.answer: Build I allows kiosks and pavilions (size 1), standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and one Petting Zoo (size 3). Build II additionally allows one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary, each size 5. The component supply has four tiles of each special enclosure type, while each zoo may have only one of each. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter play through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal; Build II is required to reach restricted-icon spaces with Build.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table lists Petting Zoo on I and Reptile House/Large Bird Aviary on II; each individual zoo may contain only one of each. Unique buildings can never be built with this action. If every space except water and rock is covered, immediately gain 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Yes: bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, or newly activated workers, may be used in later steps of that action. Resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. Immediate effects resolve at once (including before a later animal or building); after-finishing effects wait until the entire action and Action-card movement are complete. For simultaneous effects, the owning player chooses the order.
answers.evidence: X-tokens/general turn rules: bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps; resolve items one at a time and pay each item before its benefits. Animals: ordinary effects immediate, after-finishing effects after the action. Multiple simultaneous effects: owning player chooses order.

answers.answer: To play an animal, meet all card conditions, pay its full cost, and house it legally. A partner zoo on a matching continent reduces cost by 3 money for each continent icon on the animal (so two icons reduce it by 6); money from the animal's effects comes later. Most animals use an empty standard enclosure at least as large as the printed requirement, which is flipped to occupied and normally houses one animal. Petting Zoo animals must use the Petting Zoo. Reptiles and some birds may use the indicated special enclosure if it has enough free spaces; place the indicated number of player tokens there and never flip a special enclosure. Required water/rock adjacency applies, counted by distinct adjacent hexes, and also applies when using a special enclosure. Resolve ordinary effects immediately before proceeding to another animal; defer after-finishing effects until the whole Animals action and card movement are complete.
answers.evidence: Animals action: pay cost; matching partner zoo reduces it by 3 money per continent icon. Standard enclosures flip occupied; special enclosures use player tokens and are never flipped. Water/rock requirements apply to special enclosures too. Effects resolve immediately except ‘after finishing’ effects.

answers.answer: Animals II allows animals from the display within reputation range, with an additional cost equal to the folder number; the two animals may be any mix of hand and display. The display is not replenished until the turn ends. At strength 5+, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, raising your range before choosing display animals. Animals with upgrade-required conditions may also be played.
answers.evidence: Animals Side II: may play from display within reputation range, paying folder number; 2 animals may be any mix of hand/display; at strength 5+ increase reputation by 1 at the very beginning; may play animals with upgrade-required icon.

answers.answer: Only immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built may you move eligible corresponding animals that fit, choosing separately for each; relocation is available once at construction per building. Check terrain adjacency and free capacity. Mark each moved animal's indicated number of spaces with your player tokens. To free its standard enclosure, flip the smallest occupied one meeting all its requirements, including terrain; if none does, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size, flip none. The text says to move all suitable animals that fit, but does not give a separate fixed numeric cap beyond available special-enclosure capacity.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals: only immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built, relocate all corresponding eligible animals that fit, choosing each separately; check terrain adjacency and available capacity. Add indicated player tokens. Flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting all requirements, else smallest meeting size, else none.

answers.answer: The four task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, and conservation project work 5. Association I performs exactly one task; II performs one or more different tasks whose total task value is no greater than action strength. Each task needs active worker(s): normally 1, but if you already have 1 worker on that task you must place 2; with 3 already there you cannot perform it again until after a break. Other players' workers on the task do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association Side I: exactly one task, active worker required; if 1 of your workers is already on the task, place 2; if 3 are there, cannot repeat until break; other players' workers do not matter. Tasks list strengths 2/3/4/5. Side II: one or more different tasks, total value may not exceed strength; 1 or 2 workers per task.

answers.answer: Take partner zoos and universities from the Association board and place each on the lowest empty corresponding space on your zoo map; take any printed space bonus immediately, and take a university's printed reputation when acquiring it. You cannot take a duplicate university. Partner zoos must be from different continents, with at most 4 total; the third and fourth require Association II. Matching partner zoos discount animal costs by 3 per matching continent icon and provide that continent icon. The hand-limit university raises the break hand limit from 3 to 5; other universities leave it at 3. The tiles replenish after breaks. Bonuses that award a partner zoo or university also take an available tile from the board.
answers.evidence: Association tasks: gain partner zoo/university from the board onto the lowest empty map space and take printed bonus; cannot take duplicate university; partner zoos must be different continents, max 4, third/fourth needs upgraded Association. University table gives hand-limit university as 3 to 5. FAQ: bonus takes an available Association-board tile.

answers.answer: Through Association conservation project work (strength 5), support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately; Association II also permits playing a new card from the in-range display for its folder-number cost. New cards go above the Association board at the left, pushing others right; the display holds up to 2, 3, or 4 cards by player count. To support, fulfill an unoccupied condition/reward level and place one player token from the left edge of your map on it. A level is unavailable if any player's token is already there, and you normally support each project only once. Removing the map token activates its bonus immediately; take it before or after the project reward. If a new project overflows the row, discard the rightmost card and return tokens on it to their owners' supplies, while their map bonuses remain activated.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work: support in-play or play a card and support it; Association II can use display within range at folder cost. New card goes leftmost above board, pushing right; limits depend on player count. Support condition must have no token; one token total per level and normally one support per project. Overflow tokens return to owners' supplies, not maps.

answers.answer: A Release into the Wild project matches an animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement to a size band, not necessarily a single exact size: 2− accepts size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. Discard the animal and lose its icons; first lose only its printed appeal, before gaining conservation. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. Playing a new Release project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. To free space, if the animal could live in a special enclosure, remove its indicated special-enclosure tokens first if possible; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, then fall back to the smallest meeting size alone, or flip none if none meets size.
answers.evidence: Release projects: printed standard-enclosure requirement matches 2−=size 1 or 2, 3=size 3, 4+=size 4 or 5; lose printed appeal before conservation, discard animal/icons, retain conservation, reputation and ability-generated appeal. New project gives 1 reputation. Remove special-enclosure tokens if possible; otherwise flip the smallest standard meeting all requirements, fallback to size.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 card from hand if strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Sponsors II plays one or more cards if strength +1 is at least the sum of their levels; cards resolve one by one, each card's immediate effects (except after-finishing effects) fully resolving before the next. On II, cards may come from hand or from the display within reputation range, paying the folder number; no refill until turn end. If using the break-money option, I advances the Break token by strength and pays that much money, even if fewer steps remain; II pays twice that money.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I: one hand card with strength at least level, OR advance Break by strength and take that much money even if token needs fewer steps. Sponsors II: one or more, strength +1 at least total levels; resolve effects before next; display within range costs folder number; break option pays money twice.

answers.answer: Break order: discard down to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university); clear Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens; recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, slide cards down and refill; take income; reset the Break token. Kiosk income is 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, and pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count, but empty special enclosures do. Income is usually simultaneous; when effects require order, start with the break initiator (or affected player closest to them) and proceed clockwise. For players receiving display cards during income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator/first affected player and refill after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure items 1–6 list the steps and limit. Kiosk income lists qualifying neighbors and excludes empty standard enclosure but includes empty special enclosure. Income ordering says start with break initiator/first affected clockwise; refill display after each player who takes a display card.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus token next to that space; the 5-money option remains if tokens are gone. The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, all discard one before final scoring. The game ends at the end of your own turn or during a break if your Appeal and Conservation counters are in the same scoring area or have passed one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger the end unless another player triggers it first. If triggered at the end of a turn, the triggering player completes that turn and all others take one more; if during a break, everyone takes one more. Each Final Scoring card can award at most 4 conservation. Victory Points equal your appeal minus the lowest appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive score wins; ties go to the player with most conservation projects supported, then tied players share the victory.
answers.evidence: Conservation milestones list rewards at 2, 5, 8, 10 and fallback discard. End-game section gives same-scoring-area/pass trigger, timing for appeal on another player's turn, final-turn rules, four-point cap, VP formula and tiebreak.
